prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active form, which made possible incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single prize part for B044 with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. Round 1 did not shake the scientific case. Every member who addressed maturity found it mature, and the chain is complete: proglucagon processing and human incretin physiology (Holst), the truncated active peptide (Mojsov), receptor biology, GLP-2 and translation (Drucker), then independent randomized outcome evidence in diabetes, obesity and cardiovascular and renal disease. The three names map onto three separable, necessary steps. The discussion did sharpen how I would word the record. The citation should say that the discoveries made incretin-based treatment possible, so that leaving out Knudsen reads as a consequence of the discovery framing and the three-person cap, not as a verdict that long-acting analogue design was minor.
statement.case_against: Attribution remains the real weakness, and round 1 did not remove it. Habener and others sit outside the supplied credited names, Mojsov's priority is publicly contested, and Knudsen's acylated long-acting analogue work is what turned a peptide with a half-life of minutes into a drug. Any three-name set leaves someone out whose contribution mattered. The risk that a prize this visible is read as honouring a commercial product, not a mechanism, also remains. I judge these costs real but smaller than the costs of the alternatives: swapping a discovery name for Knudsen weakens the discovery claim, and the other candidates carry attribution gaps of their own (Eshhar for B018, six names for B001, mammalian branches for B012).

responses.point: Perlmann argues that Mojsov's contested public role is a reason to read the primary record carefully, not to drop her, because peptide identification is distinct from Holst's physiology and Drucker's biology.
responses.response: I agree with the method, and it answers the chair's question about evidence. What I can rely on is the supplied record, which credits Mojsov specifically with identifying and synthesizing the biologically active GLP-1(7-36) form, and I cannot adjudicate priority beyond that from these files. Public dispute alone is not evidence against her. I would keep her at full weight on that basis, and I would state in the record that Habener's early proglucagon and GLP-1 work is acknowledged and that the supplied credited list may be incomplete. I also hold to my round-1 point that if the committee wanted Knudsen in the citation, one of the three discovery names would have to go, and I see no attribution argument for dropping any of them.

responses.point: Linnarsson would exclude Knudsen only because of the three-person limit and the discovery focus, and wants the citation wording to credit the translation to therapy so the omission is not read as a judgement on her work.
responses.response: I now agree with this and have adopted it. The citation I propose names the discoveries and says they made incretin-based treatment possible, so the translation is acknowledged without crediting the industrial development step as a prize achievement. I would add that the committee should be willing to say openly that the exclusion is a cost. I also accept your point that B012 is better as a pairing with a clinically proven achievement than as a substitute for GLP-1. That is a reason to think about a two-part design, but not this year, because the three-person budget is spent on B044.

responses.point: The chair holds that a two-part prize would need a different three-person budget, and asks whether any member wants a second part alongside B044 and whether the cap leaves room.
responses.response: My answer is no second part this year. With Drucker, Holst and Mojsov the cap is exhausted, and every candidate that could be a second part brings an unresolved credit problem: B018 lacks Eshhar and has a partial fit for Rosenberg, B001 has six names for the seats, and B012 would need Ron, Harding and Kaufman for the mammalian branches. Dropping a B044 name to make room would damage the strongest case to improve a weaker one. I accept the chair's point that B012 and B018 answer different questions. If I had to choose a second part, I would take B018 for its clinical proof, with a stated reservation about Eshhar, but I would not build the preferred configuration on it.

responses.point: Sandberg calls CAR-T the strongest challenger and the best second part, ranks the unfolded protein response below it because its therapeutic relevance is still developing, and questions whether Rosenberg belongs in a CAR-specific citation.
responses.response: I partly move toward you. On impact I accept that B018 has the stronger demonstrated clinical effect, and it is relevant to my own field, because CAR-T is now being tried in refractory lupus and other autoimmune disease. I disagree that the Eshhar gap is a small problem. With Eshhar outside the credited names, a June, Sadelain, Rosenberg trio cannot be defended as the CAR-specific discovery, and a citation limited to June and Sadelain would still not credit the chimeric receptor concept. That is why I keep B012 ahead as the cleaner alternative, while I list B018 second because the clinical case is stronger. I would not call either of them a second part this year.

responses.point: El-Manira reaches the same three names with less confidence than the others, defends leaving out Knudsen only on the narrow ground that the prize rewards the discovery of the physiological principle, and says we must be prepared to explain that choice.
responses.response: I accept that framing and think it is the honest one. My explanation, if the committee must give one, is that the prize recognizes the discovery of a physiological principle and the identification of the active molecule, and that the drug-design step that made weekly agonists possible rests on that discovery. I would also not call the credited trio the settled historical record. The citation should be built on what the supplied evidence supports, and the uncertainty should be recorded, not hidden. I disagree only mildly with your suggestion that B012 would be a strong second part: I agree its medical link is indirect, which is why I treat it as an alternative and not as a pairing.

uncertainties: How much weight Habener's early work should carry, given that he is not on the supplied credited list and I cannot verify the historical record beyond the supplied names.
Whether the citation wording alone is enough to prevent Knudsen's exclusion from being read as a verdict on her contribution.
Whether the committee would accept a second part in a later year, and which of B012 or B018 could then be configured fairly.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. My autoimmunity field overlaps with CAR-T for autoimmune disease (B018) and with cGAS-STING (B040), but I have no documented personal or institutional tie to any credited person on the shortlist, including the B044 names. A shared Karolinska setting with colleagues is not a conflict. I do not request recusal.
